identity.name: Marcellinus' Dalmatia
alt_names: Dalmatia under Marcellinus and Julius Nepos

land.text: Dalmatia: Marcellinus 'ruled over the region of Dalmatia', where his fleet was 'based at Salona'; Nepos 'ruled Dalmatia from Salona, the provincial capital'

predecessors.note: The western-roman-empire dossier has no Dalmatia loss in 454; Cliopatria's Western Roman Empire shapes keep Dalmatia. The Marcellinus page: he 'rebelled against Western Emperor Valentinian III' in 454 and pledged allegiance to Majorian in December 457.

land.text: Dalmatia, joined to the Western Empire when Julius Nepos was proclaimed western Augustus on 24 June 474; he fled back to Salona on 28 August 475

successors.note: The western-roman-empire dossier moves its capital and shape to Salona/Dalmatia in 476 and ends in 480; Dalmatia was then Odoacer's from late 481 or 482.

capitals.name: Salona (Solin)
capitals.note: Marcellinus's fleet was 'based at Salona' (Marcellinus page, which names no capital); Nepos 'ruled Dalmatia from Salona, the provincial capital' (Julius Nepos page).

rulers.name: Marcellinus
rulers.title: comes rei militaris, later magister militum and patrician
rulers.note: 'records first mention his name in 454 when he rebelled against Western Emperor Valentinian III'; 'He appears to have remained ruler of Dalmatia down to 468'; murdered in Sicily in 468, 'possibly by Ricimer's order'.

rulers.name: Julius Nepos
rulers.title: magister militum of Dalmatia (western emperor 474-475)
rulers.note: 'Succeeds his uncle Marcellinus as the semi-autonomous governor of Dalmatia' in 468; first attested as magister militum on 1 June 473; Western Roman Emperor from 24 June 474; flees to Salona on 28 August 475.

correction.text: Dalmatia: Marcellinus 'ruled over the region of Dalmatia', where his fleet was 'based at Salona'; Nepos 'ruled Dalmatia from Salona, the provincial capital'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives no extent beyond 'the region of Dalmatia', with a naval base at Salona and lead and iron resources; Julius Nepos page: 'semi-autonomous governor of Dalmatia'. The gazetteer's Dalmatia region (12 thousand km2) is the coast; the Roman province reached inland. The 464-468 campaigns of Marcellinus in Sicily and Sardinia ('expelled the Vandals from Sicily' and 'retaken Sardinia' by 468) were fought as a Roman commander and are not part of his realm. No area on either page.

region.text: Dalmatia: Marcellinus 'ruled over the region of Dalmatia', where his fleet was 'based at Salona'; Nepos 'ruled Dalmatia from Salona, the provincial capital'

ledger.note: 454: Marcellinus rebels against Valentinian III and holds Dalmatia. The page 'records first mention his name in 454 when he rebelled against Western Emperor Valentinian III'; 'He appears to have remained ruler of Dalmatia down to 468'; he is 'believed to have held the title of comes rei militaris'. The page gives no takeover date; 454 is the first mention. When Majorian took the throne in December 457 'Marcellinus pledged his allegiance to the new emperor'.

468: Marcellinus is murdered and his nephew Julius Nepos inherits Dalmatia. 'Marcellinus was murdered in Sicily that same year, possibly by Ricimer's order'; Nepos 'Succeeds his uncle Marcellinus as the semi-autonomous governor of Dalmatia' in 468 and 'may have held this post from Marcellinus's death'. The state and its land continue under the same family.

region.text: Dalmatia, which joins the Western Empire when its ruler Nepos becomes western Augustus

ledger.note: 24 June 474: Nepos, ruler of Dalmatia, deposes Glycerius and is proclaimed western Augustus in Rome, so Dalmatia ceases to be separate from the Western Empire. Julius Nepos page: 'On 24 June, having deposed Glycerius, Nepos was proclaimed the western Augustus in Rome'; infobox 'In Italy: 24 June 474 - 28 August 475', 'In Dalmatia: 28 August 475 - 9 May 480'. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: moved from 28 August 475, the date Nepos fled to Salona; the author's own note said Dalmatia ceased to be separate when Nepos became emperor in 474. The western-roman-empire dossier needs the matching 474 gain of Dalmatia.] He was murdered near Salona on 9 May 480 and Odoacer took Dalmatia in 'late 481 or 482'.

wars.name: Marcellinus's campaigns against the Vandals (Sicily and Sardinia)
wars.outcome: 'In 464 or 465 Marcellinus returned to Sicily to defend the island against the Vandals'; by 468 he had 'expelled the Vandals from Sicily' and 'retaken Sardinia'; he 'never sailed for Africa' in the 468 campaign and was murdered in Sicily that year.
wars.note: Fought as a Roman commander; the western-roman-empire dossier carries Sicily (gain 459, loss 462). Majorian's planned attack on Vandal Africa 'was defeated before it began', undated.

certainty.note: The pages name the region, not a frontier.

sources.title: Marcellinus (magister militum)
sources.note: 454 rebellion, ruler of Dalmatia to 468, Salona fleet, Sicily and Sardinia, 468 murder.

sources.title: Julius Nepos
sources.note: 468 succession, 473 magister militum, 474 emperor, 28 August 475 flight to Salona, 480 murder, 481/482 Odoacer.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (Cliopatria's Western Roman Empire shapes keep Dalmatia throughout). Two pages opened. The Marcellinus page calls him 'ruler of Dalmatia' and never 'king'; Nepos's title is magister militum of Dalmatia (attested 1 June 473) and the pages call his post 'semi-autonomous governor'. Whether Dalmatia was independent or a nominal part of the Western Empire is therefore a judgment: the map should draw it as a Roman successor-in-fact. The dossier ends on 24 June 474, when Nepos became western Augustus (reviewer eu-04-x moved it from 28 August 475); the western-roman-empire dossier takes Salona as capital from 476 to 480 and needs a 474 gain of Dalmatia. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: Dalmatia is a coastal region only; Illyricum and Pannonia are not names.
